title: Kansas police chief used Flock license plate cameras 164 times to track ex-girlfriend

reading.body:
This is not a failure of the license plate reader's matching or recognition. It is a misuse of a working system by the person authorised to query it. The access was legitimate, the queries were not, and the harm came from the operator rather than the software.

Catching it would have required oversight at the query layer rather than the camera layer. Someone would have needed to review who was running lookups, how often, and against whom, and to treat a repeated pattern of checks on one person as a signal. A supervisor approving or auditing individual queries could have seen the concentration. Nothing in the reporting establishes that any such review existed.

The reporting comes from a single outlet and rests on a Kansas certification order. The headline and the summary give different counts of the camera checks, 164 and 228, and which figure is correct is not established. Whether any criminal charge or prosecution followed the resignation and the loss of certification is also not established.

reports.title: Kansas police chief used Flock license plate cameras 164 times to track ex-girlfriend

summary: In Sedgwick, Kansas, Police Chief Lee Nygaard reportedly used Flock Safety license plate readers 228 times from June to October 2023 to check where his ex-girlfriend and her new boyfriend were, according to a Kansas certification order. The order said he also followed them in a police vehicle and admitted jealousy influenced his actions. Nygaard resigned in October 2023 and later lost his police certification.
